title: International Economics Adventure 3: Trade Blocs & WTO
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace the ladder from a free trade area to monetary union and meet the WTO.

concepts.def: Free trade area — no internal tariffs
Switch from costly home to cheap partner
Switch from cheap non-member to costly member

walkthroughs.body_html:
Five rungs of trade integration.

1. FTA — no internal tariffs (e.g. USMCA).
2. Customs union — common external tariff (Mercosur).
3. Common market — free movement of goods, labour, capital (EU Single Market).
4. Monetary union — shared currency (Eurozone).
5. Political/economic union — common policy.

Trade creation: tariffs fall, members switch from costly home producers to cheaper partners — welfare ↑.

Trade diversion: a previously cheaper non-member is now blocked by the common tariff — welfare ↓.

Net welfare depends on which effect dominates.

The World Trade Organization (1995, succeeding GATT 1947) sets multilateral rules.

Core principles: most-favoured nation, national treatment, tariff binding, dispute settlement.

Doha round (2001) on development largely stalled; the Appellate Body is currently paralysed.
